# Overview

`MiR_ORA()` performs miRNA enrichment analysis by testing the overlap
between a set of differentially expressed miRNAs and each pathway's
miRNA set. Pathway definitions only specify genes, so the pathway miRNA
set is derived from the pathway gene set through `background_MGI`. This
is a standard over-representation analysis, built on
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("clusterProfiler")`'s `enricher()`.

This vignette uses the same toy BLCA example data as the package's main
Quick Start vignette. See `vignette("miREA")` for a description of that
data and for running all nine methods together through `miREA()`.

# Required inputs

* `pathway`, a two column data frame with columns `pathway` and `gene`.
* `mir_DEdata`, a four column data frame with columns `miRNA`,
  `log2FoldChange`, `stat`, and `padj`.
* `background_MGI`, a two column data frame with columns `miRNA` and
  `gene`, or `NULL` to use the bundled default (see `vignette("miREA")`,
  Step 1, for details on `background_MGI`).
* `background` for `MiR_ORA()` itself, a character vector of background
  miRNAs. If left `NULL`, `MiR_ORA()` falls back to all mature miRNAs in
  miRBase version 22.

```{r load-data}
library(miREA)
data(toy_pathway)
data(toy_mir_DEdata)
data(toy_gene_DEdata)
data(background_MGI)
```

# Run MiR-ORA

```{r prepare-input}
input_data <- getAllInputData(
    methods = "MiR_ORA",
    pathway = toy_pathway,
    mir_DEdata = toy_mir_DEdata,
    gene_DEdata = toy_gene_DEdata,
    background_MGI = background_MGI
)
```

`input_data$data$MiR_ORA` holds the differentially expressed miRNAs,
built by `getAllInputData()`. `input_data$pathway$MiR` holds the pathway
miRNA sets, derived from `toy_pathway`'s genes through `background_MGI`.

```{r run-mir-ora}
res <- MiR_ORA(
    DEmiR = input_data$data$MiR_ORA,
    background = unique(input_data$pathway$MiR$miRNA),
    pathway = input_data$pathway$MiR,
    pvalueCutoff = 1
)
head(res)
```

# Run through miREA()

`MiR_ORA()` can also be run through the `miREA()` wrapper, which is
useful when you want its result alongside other methods' results in a
single `miREAResult` object (see `vignette("miREA")`, Step 2, for the
multi-method case). For a single target, `background` can be a plain
character vector instead of a named list.

```{r run-through-miREA}
result <- miREA(
    methods = "MiR_ORA",
    input_data = input_data,
    background = unique(input_data$pathway$MiR$miRNA),
    pvalueCutoff = 1
)
head(result$result$MiR_ORA)
```

# Supplying your own miRNA list

If you already have a list of differentially expressed miRNAs from an
external analysis instead of letting `getAllInputData()` derive one from
`mir_DEdata`, call `MiR_ORA()` directly with that list and
`input_data$pathway$MiR`.

```{r custom-list, eval=FALSE}
# replace with your own miRNA list
my_DEmiR <- c("hsa-miR-21-5p", "hsa-miR-155-5p")
res_custom <- MiR_ORA(
    DEmiR = my_DEmiR,
    background = unique(input_data$pathway$MiR$miRNA),
    pathway = input_data$pathway$MiR,
    pvalueCutoff = 1
)
```
